clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance on October 11, 1933, the date the order is signed ('The White House, October 11, 1933'). The order's sole operative command, 'that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants, be and it is hereby denied', is a one-time determination: once made it commands nothing further. Under the shared analysis of denials of exemption, the applicants' continuing obligation after the denial is the code's own operation, which the approving order governs and which ended with the repeal; it is not a surviving command of the denial. Actor: EO 6331-A itself. Later event: section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating the power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, which ended the code obligations the denial left in place; it does not end this order, which was spent in 1933.

research_rationale:
EO 6331-A (October 11, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) denies an application for exemption from the minimum-wage provision of the Code of Fair Competition for the Coat and Suit Industry. Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6331-the-matter-the-application-associated-cloak-and-suit-manufacturers.txt, 1,515 characters, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false). APP page check (AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, working-text paragraph): the jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with sha256 4b14b616a76238c21bf3095a2d752b9e67c2406ac7cf85e44fee4b32f818ec39 is headed 'Executive Order 6331-A—In the Matter of the Application of Associated Cloak and Suit Manufacturers of Portland, Oregon, for Certain Exemptions from the Coat and Suit Code', dated October 11, 1933, node app:node/362158, Common Crawl capture 2025-12-08T23:13:08Z; its text_sha256 f815607fc55488c2138868f082613b77edc4654a755f0eee7943cc5a180fcb9d equals the sha256 I computed for the held file, and the page heading, the date and the subject agree with the text. Cotton holds the exact page bytes (jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output/captures). Identity also agrees with the census register row and the WPA 1944 list (page 542: 'Application of the Associated Cloak and Suit Manufacturers of Portland, Oreg., for certain exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Coat and Suit Industry denied. I NRA Codes 735.'). The number 6331 is shared with an unrelated land-withdrawal order of the same day in the government printed copy (jobs/hathi-gpo-orders EO_6331); the lettered identity 6331-A and the subject come from the APP heading and the WPA list. The held text does not itself print the applicants' names ('the named applicants', 'the above-named applicants'); the heading identifies the Associated Cloak and Suit Manufacturers of Portland, Oregon, and the page record's text length (1,514 characters) matches the held text, so the representation is complete as the page gives it. The order recites that the Coat and Suit code was approved earlier on terms, that the Administrator held hearings under the President's order of July 15, 1933 on applications for exemption from the code's minimum wage, and that the Administrator's report of September 28, 1933 is adopted; it finds that 'no case of injustice and extreme hardship requiring special treatment has been made out', and orders 'that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants, be and it is hereby denied'. The machine clause inventory (one clause, characters 527 to 1477, the paragraph beginning 'It appearing to me') is complete and correct. The dossier's two own-terms leads (report_deadline) are the date of the Administrator's past report (September 28, 1933); the order sets no deadline.

savings.reason: The denial leaves nothing to carry forward as a command. What outlasted it was the applicants' subjection to the code's own minimum-wage provision, which was the approving order's operation under section 3 and ended with the repeal of June 14, 1935 (section 2 of S.J. Res. 113). Liabilities for conduct before that day under the code are accrued effects of the code (the general savings statute of the time, which is not a held source, is the ordinary ground; the repeal text contains no savings clause), not effects of this denial. The denial is a completed determination that no hardship case was made out; nothing in it continues after October 11, 1933.

source_notes.reason: Section 3(a) lets the President provide exceptions to and exemptions from a code; the denial refused one, so it created no exemption and the code's own operation (sections 3(b), (c), (f)) continued to govern the applicants until the repeal.
